{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABZZ2hKQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhDBK3A", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 49, "title": "Implement 8253 binary mode-0 initial counting, terminal IRQ0 and continued decrement", "body": "## Problem

Freshly programming PIT mode 0 does not establish the required count/OUT sequence. DOS software using a terminal-count interrupt or reading the counter afterward can observe incorrect timing, stale OUT and a permanently frozen count.

At baseline `69e60a951c1a659ab67bf535a8e4bb5b97c43383`:

- [`Pit::write`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/69e60a951c1a659ab67bf535a8e4bb5b97c43383/src/devices.rs#L326) resets counting/output state only for modes 2/3. Switching from mode 3 to mode 0 can leave OUT high and the previous counter active.
- [`Counter::write`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/69e60a951c1a659ab67bf535a8e4bb5b97c43383/src/devices.rs#L172) immediately assigns the mode-0 count instead of scheduling a separate load clock.
- [`Counter::tick`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/69e60a951c1a659ab67bf535a8e4bb5b97c43383/src/devices.rs#L230) disables mode 0 at terminal count and freezes it at zero.

Implement one bounded behavior: the mode-0 lifecycle beginning with a new mode control word, through initial loading, terminal count and subsequent counting. This supplies a basic timer/interrupt prerequisite shared by both profiles.

## Expected outcome

For binary mode 0 with GATE held high:

1. A new mode word sets OUT low and waits for the complete programmed count-byte sequence.
2. The next PIT clock loads the count without decrementing. Encoded zero represents 65,536; pre-load count readback is undefined.
3. Each subsequent clock decrements once. Reaching zero raises OUT; counting continues modulo 65,536 while OUT stays high, including across later wraps.
4. A fresh mode word starts another independent lifecycle. Ordinary count latches preserve a snapshot without stopping counting.

These semantics follow Intel’s [8253/8253-5 datasheet: Counter Loading, Mode 0 and Read/Write Procedures](https://web.cecs.pdx.edu/~mpj/llp/references/8253.pdf).

For count 4, successive `(count, OUT)` samples beginning with the load clock are `(4,L), (3,L), (2,L), (1,L), (0,H), (65535,H), (65534,H)`.

OUT0’s terminal rise feeds the existing PIC request latch. Falling transitions, held-high output and subsequent counter wraps must not produce additional requests. Lowering OUT must not erase an already latched PIC request. Follow Intel’s [8259A edge-triggered interrupt and IRR/ISR contracts](https://courses.cs.washington.edu/courses/cse451/25wi/documentation/8259A.pdf#page=17).

Scope includes all three counters, VM/Ap, existing primary/mirrored timer ports, ordinary latch reads, scheduler batching, reset and IRQ0 delivery. Preserve the existing clock conversion and fractional remainder.

Non-goals: count-only mode-0 rewrites without a new mode word, external GATE control, modes 1/4/5, active mode-3 rewrites, BCD, comprehensive latch/access corner cases, changes to beeper mixing/resampling, or exact electrical/instruction-cycle fidelity. Mode-0 audio behavior remains unverified by this Issue.

## Context and reproduction

**Source-derived reproduction; not executed by this evaluator:** construct a default `Pit`, write control `36h`, then `30h`, write channel-0 count bytes `04h,00h`, and advance five scheduler cycles. The current source leaves OUT high and decrements to 3. The required first loaded state is `(4,L)`. After terminal count, further advancement currently leaves zero instead of exposing continued decrement.

[`tests/pit.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/69e60a951c1a659ab67bf535a8e4bb5b97c43383/tests/pit.rs) supplies useful independent trace, fractional-clock, PIC/CPU and original guest-probe patterns for modes 2/3. Add mode-0 acceptance without weakening those assertions.

**Project progress:** PR #48 completed the bounded mode-3 improvement. The Coordinator reports 22 PIT tests, 182 native integration tests and 70 production-Wasm browser tests passing, including twelve original-probe boots. The [validation record](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/69e60a951c1a659ab67bf535a8e4bb5b97c43383/docs/validation.md#issue-47-8253-binary-mode-3-2026-10-23) records those results and the alternate browser ports. Independent review and remote CI success are unestablished. This evaluation inspected source/diffs/reports and ran no builds or tests. Supplied open Issues are empty; recent completed improvements do not cover mode 0.

All 26 fixed inventory scopes and statuses remain unchanged:

- **Partial:** cpu-v30, cpu386, protected-mode, memory, pic, pit, dma, keyboard, mouse, fdc, gdc, egc, pegc, text-cg, display-timing, opn, opna, bios, lio, integration.
- **Unimplemented:** paging, fpu, rtc.
- **Implemented, unverified:** ide, grcg, pcm86.

PIT remains partial after this Issue. Its remaining work includes the excluded rewrite/gate/mode/BCD/latch/audio behavior above and divisor-1 behavior in modes 2/3. Protected execution, paging and basic FPU remain required project goals. Limited probes and six-game reports do not establish full hardware accuracy or commercial compatibility.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Implement the scoped lifecycle in original Rust. Add an explicit specification-derived trace regression covering the reproduction, counts 1/2/4/65,535/encoded-zero, all channels and supported byte-loading forms. Assert the Expected outcome, including post-terminal readback and repeated wraps.
- [ ] Test incomplete initial pairs, a separate load clock, completed ordinary latch reads across terminal count, and fresh mode-word transitions between mode 0 and modes 2/3. Verify channel isolation and reset during partial programming, pending load and post-terminal counting. Do not assert undefined pre-load count values.
- [ ] Compare single-clock progression with irregular batches, zero advancement, preserved fractional clocks and split versus unsplit `u32::MAX` scheduler-cycle advancement. Final state and aggregate edge reports must agree; large advances must use bounded arithmetic.
- [ ] Through both timer port banks on VM/Ap, verify IRQ0 masking, retained IRR, acknowledgement, ISR/EOI and absence of repeated requests after terminal count. Include CPU IF-clear/HLT followed by delivery, EOI and IRET. Account separately for pre-existing mode-2/3 programming edges.
- [ ] Add an original MIT assembly boot probe with reproducible offline preparation and a manifest recording source/image hashes, license, exact guest-owned results/guards and a fixed maximum budget of 2,000,000 scheduler slots per boot. The guest must demonstrate advancing post-terminal counter reads and exactly one hardware IRQ0 per arming, then rearm using a fresh mode word. Bound guest waits and check for unwanted additional IRQs during continued counting. Hosts may only boot, step and inspect; no IRQ injection or result fabrication.
- [ ] Run the identical source-built image natively and through production-release Wasm on VM/Ap, before/after reset, at both browser URL roots. Require exact results/guards, PASS without FAIL, unchanged disk bytes and no core/browser errors. Demonstrate that the focused reproduction and guest probe fail against the stated baseline and pass with the change.
- [ ] Wire fixture preparation into existing CI and document commands, provenance, hardware scope and actual results. Use original/licensed sources only; no commercial ROM acquisition or copied emulator implementation. Evaluator-local missing fixtures are not a project-level blocker.
- [ ] The Coordinator prepares existing legal fixtures and runs `cargo test --locked --test pit`, `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `git diff --check` and the README production-Wasm/browser workflow ending in `npm test`. Preserve existing PIT, PIC/SMM, BIOS timer, CPU-shadow, DOS/application, VM and game assertions and execution budgets. Report failures, skips and any equivalent port-only browser configuration honestly; do not treat omitted required checks as acceptance.

## Optional validation

None.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
